Sequential WJP Color Scales

Source: R/utils.R
scale_fill_wjp_seq.Rd

scale_fill_wjp_seq() and scale_colour_wjp_seq() map a continuous variable to a sequential scale between two WJP colors. The colors are mixed linearly in RGB space, as in the cards and networks of WJP country reports.

Usage

scale_fill_wjp_seq(
  low = wjp_colors()[["card_low"]],
  high = wjp_colors()[["main"]],
  ...,
  na.value = "#ffffff",
  guide = "colourbar",
  aesthetics = "fill"
)

scale_colour_wjp_seq(
  low = wjp_colors()[["card_low"]],
  high = wjp_colors()[["main"]],
  ...,
  na.value = "#ffffff",
  guide = "colourbar",
  aesthetics = "colour"
)

scale_color_wjp_seq(
  low = wjp_colors()[["card_low"]],
  high = wjp_colors()[["main"]],
  ...,
  na.value = "#ffffff",
  guide = "colourbar",
  aesthetics = "colour"
)

Arguments

low, high

Colors of the low and high ends of the scale. Defaults to the report colors card_low and main (see wjp_colors()).

...

Other arguments passed to ggplot2::continuous_scale(), such as name, limits, breaks, and labels.

na.value

Color for missing values.

guide

Guide for the scale. Default is "colourbar".

aesthetics

Aesthetics the scale applies to.

Value

A ggplot2 scale.

Examples

library(ggplot2)

grid <- expand.grid(x = 1:5, y = 1:3)
grid$value <- seq(0, 100, length.out = nrow(grid))

ggplot(grid, aes(x, y, fill = value)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_wjp_seq()
